Daily Brief

The day's most significant developments center on escalating tensions in the US-Iran conflict, with American forces firing missiles to disable a cargo ship attempting to breach the Iran blockade [BBC, The Hindu], while revelations emerged that President Trump secretly switched aircraft after the NATO summit due to credible Iranian threats [BBC]. In Colombia, rescue operations continue following Monday's magnitude 7.4 earthquake, with the death toll rising above 180 and potentially exceeding 240 [BBC, Le Monde, RFI]. The Russia-Ukraine conflict intensified with deadly strikes exchanged by both sides—Ukraine hit oil infrastructure deep in Tatarstan, killing 13, while Russia struck Zaporizhzhia with what Kyiv claims were North Korean missiles [BBC, Al Jazeera]. In a significant political development, Hungary's parliament elected András Baka as president, a judge previously removed by Viktor Orbán, signaling continued dismantling of the former prime minister's legacy [BBC]. Meanwhile, Russia's only anti-war party, Yabloko, was barred from parliamentary elections by a Moscow court, effectively eliminating opposition voices ahead of next month's vote [BBC].

Top Stories
01 Conflict

US Helicopter Fires Missiles to Disable Cargo Ship Attempting to Break Iran Blockade

  • US Central Command confirmed an MH-60 helicopter fired two Hellfire missiles into the engine room of the Panama-flagged M/V Vela Nova in the Gulf of Oman on Tuesday
  • The ship's civilian crew reportedly ignored repeated warnings from American forces; the vessel is no longer transiting to Iran
  • This marks the third time the US has forcibly halted a vessel since reinstating the Iran ports blockade on July 14, having redirected 55 ships and boarded two others
  • Iran has effectively closed the Strait of Hormuz since the war began, causing wild fluctuations in global oil prices

02 Geopolitics

Trump Confirms Secret Aircraft Switch After NATO Summit Due to Iranian Missile Threat

  • President Trump confirmed he secretly switched from Air Force One to a military aircraft when departing the NATO summit in Turkey on July 8 due to a possible threat
  • US intelligence detected a credible Iranian threat to fire a missile at the plane; reports indicate a person near the summit was seen with a shoulder-fired missile
  • Trump was hidden in a catering truck and transported to an alternate aircraft while journalists and staff remained on the decoy Air Force One
  • The president has previously stated he was Iran's 'number one target' and drew connections between the threat and his February decision to launch military action against Iran

03 Climate

Colombia Earthquake Death Toll Rises Past 180 as Rescue Efforts Continue

  • A magnitude 7.4 earthquake struck western Colombia at 07:34 local time Monday, with the epicenter near San José del Palmar in Choco department
  • Official death toll stands at 181, though aggregated local figures suggest over 240 deaths; nearly 2,600 injured and approximately 200 missing
  • President Abelardo de la Espriella declared a state of emergency just three days after being sworn in; over 1,100 homes destroyed and 8,000 damaged
  • France, EU, US ($15.5 million), Israel, Mexico, and Ecuador have offered assistance; a 32-year-old woman was pulled alive from rubble on Tuesday

04 Conflict

Ukraine and Russia Exchange Deadly Strikes as Kyiv Claims Moscow Using North Korean Missiles

  • At least 13 people, including one child and seven Uzbek citizens, were killed in Ukrainian drone strikes on Tatarstan, more than 1,100 km from the border—one of the deadliest single attacks on Russia since 2022
  • Ukraine's military confirmed hitting the Tanevo oil refinery in Nizhnekamsk during the hours-long overnight strike
  • Russian strikes on Zaporizhzhia killed seven people and injured at least 24; President Zelensky claimed these involved North Korean ballistic missiles
  • Zelensky stated Ukraine has sent new peace proposals to the United States and warned Russia cannot wage war without North Korean reinforcements

05 Policy

Hungary Elects Judge Previously Removed by Orbán as New President

  • Parliament elected András Baka, 73, a former Supreme Court head whom Viktor Orbán had removed from his position, as Hungary's new president by a vote of 140-6
  • All 51 MPs from Orbán's Fidesz party walked out before the vote in protest against the ousting of their preferred candidate Tamás Sulyok
  • Baka will oversee the writing of a new constitution to replace Orbán's 2011 version and monitor PM Péter Magyar's efforts to dismantle Orbán's political and economic structures
  • The new Magyar government has passed 27 laws and two constitutional amendments since taking office in May, canceling all states of emergency Orbán used to govern by decree
